title: Havne signal file
description: A Havne signal file (format 1, ADR-0051): a set of your own signals, read from a module's replies or computed from other signals. Map this schema to your files in your editor's settings: the loader refuses a "$schema" key, as it refuses every key it doesn't know.
$comment: The loader (core/src/signal_file.cpp) is the truth; tests/schema_keys.py keeps each object's keys equal to its only_keys sets. The loader alone checks: "havne_signals" as the first key; a file's size (1 MiB) and its JSON's rules (duplicate keys, depth 32); lengths in UTF-8 bytes (a schema counts characters, so non-ASCII text can pass here and be refused there); whole numbers written with no fraction or exponent (1.0 and 1e0 are refused); the profile name made from "name" ("user." and the name in lower case, other runs of characters one "-") at most 63 characters; ECU ids and rx IDs given once each, a tx of the same width as its rx, one ID width across the file's ECUs and the base set's (obd2's are 11-bit), at most 4 ECUs with the base set's, an rx shared with the base set sharing its tx too; a signal's "ecu" listed in "ecus", and an ECU for every signal that reads a reply; signal keys given once each; a field ending within a reply's 4096 bytes; an enum's raw values within its field's bits; an expression's grammar (+ - * /, parentheses, unary minus, decimal constants, signals by key), its inputs (signals of the file that are neither computed nor text, or obd2.<key> with "extends": "obd2"), at most 4 inputs, 16 constants, 16 operations and 16 levels of nesting; "max_age" naming only inputs its expression reads; the signal set's validator; at most 256 requests with the base set's.

havne_signals.title: Format
havne_signals.description: The signal-file format's version, and the file's first key. This Havne reads format 1.

name.title: Name
name.description: The file's name, 1 to 63 bytes with at least one letter or digit. Its profile is "user." and the name in lower case, every other run of characters one "-" ("Daily driver extras" is user.daily-driver-extras).

signals.title: Signals
signals.description: The file's signals, 1 to 1024. An expression may read a signal listed after it.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Free text for the reader of the file, allowed in every object the loader checks keys in. JSON has no comments: a "notes" string goes where one would.

tool.description: A key starting "x-" is a tool's own: the loader skips it and what it holds.

displayText.$comment: The formula guard (ADR-0049 section 8): a recording's CSV can't hold text a spreadsheet would run as a formula

key.title: Key
key.description: The signal's stable name, 1 to 31 of a-z, 0-9 and _. Expressions and fixtures name a signal by it, since its place in the list sets its id.

hexId.description: A CAN ID in hex, 1 to 8 digits, 1 to 1FFFFFFF.

extends.title: Extends
extends.description: A built-in set the file adds to: its signals and ECUs come first, the file's after. Only "obd2" in format 1. Without it the file is a set of its own.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the file's signals come from. Every copy of the file keeps it, so the file carries its attribution.

name.title: Source name
name.description: Who or what the signals come from, 1 to 512 bytes.

url.title: URL
url.description: Where the source can be found, 1 to 512 bytes.

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: The source's revision the signals were taken from, 1 to 512 bytes.

license.title: License
license.description: The source's license, an SPDX identifier where it has one, 1 to 512 bytes.

modified.title: Modified
modified.description: What the file changes from the source, 1 to 512 bytes.

ecus.title: ECUs
ecus.description: The modules the file's signals read, the base set's counted toward 4 in all, of one ID width.

ecu.title: ECU
ecu.description: A module by the ID it replies on and the ID it's asked on.

id.title: ECU id
id.description: The name a signal's "ecu" gives it, 1 to 31 of a-z, 0-9 and _.

rx.title: Reply ID
rx.description: The CAN ID the module replies on, in hex: 11-bit (7E8) or 29-bit (18DAF110).

tx.title: Request ID
tx.description: The CAN ID the module is asked on, in hex, of the rx's width. It may be left out only where the standard gives it: rx - 8 for 7E8 to 7EF, and the 18DA swap for 18DAF1xx.

read.title: Read
read.description: The request whose reply holds the signal: a Service 01 PID or a Service 22 DID.

service.title: Service
service.description: "01" for an OBD-II PID, "22" for a DID (UDS ReadDataByIdentifier).

number.title: PID or DID
number.description: The PID in 2 hex digits (service 01) or the DID in 4 (service 22).

byte.title: Byte
byte.description: The field's first byte among the reply's data bytes after the echo: 0 is J1979's A.

bits.title: Bits
bits.description: The field's width in bits, 1 to 32. A big-endian field takes whole bytes.

bit.title: Bit
bit.description: The field's first bit in its first byte, 0 to 7: a little-endian field's only.

order.title: Byte order
order.description: "be" (big-endian, as both services send) or "le" (little-endian, for a bit field).

wholeBytes.$comment: A big-endian field is whole bytes: bits a multiple of 8 and no bit

numberField.title: Field
numberField.description: Where a number signal's raw value sits in the reply.

signed.title: Signed
signed.description: Whether the raw value is two's complement.

enumField.title: Field
enumField.description: Where an enum signal's raw value sits in the reply, unsigned.

textField.title: Field
textField.description: Where a text or hex signal's bytes sit in the reply.

bytes.title: Bytes
bytes.description: How many bytes the text takes; 0 (the default) runs to the reply's end.

signalName.title: Name
signalName.description: The name shown for the signal, 1 to 31 bytes, not starting with = + - @, a tab or a CR.

signalEcu.title: ECU
signalEcu.description: The id of the ECU the signal reads, one of "ecus". Left out, the first of "ecus", or the base set's first.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: The value's unit, 0 to 15 bytes, not starting with = + - @, a tab or a CR. A unit outside Havne's conversion table is shown as written and never converted.

group.title: Group
group.description: The part of the car the signal belongs to; left out, other.

plot.title: Plot rank
plot.description: The signal's place among those a chart plots first: 1 first, 0 (the default) unranked.

signal.title: Signal
signal.description: One signal: a number (the default kind), an enum, text or hex read from a reply, or a value computed from other signals.

allOf.$comment: A DID's echo is a byte longer than a PID's, so its field starts a byte earlier at the latest

numberSignal.title: Number signal
numberSignal.description: A number read from a reply: the raw field times scale, plus offset.

scale.title: Scale
scale.description: What one raw count is worth, never 0.

enumSignal.title: Enum signal
enumSignal.description: A raw value read from a reply and shown by its label; a value with no label shows as its number.

values.title: Values
values.description: Each raw value, in decimal with no leading zero, to its label: at most 256.

additionalProperties.title: Label
additionalProperties.description: The raw value's label, 1 to 27 bytes, not starting with = + - @, a tab or a CR.

textSignal.title: Text signal
textSignal.description: Bytes read from a reply and shown as ASCII ("text") or as hex pairs ("hex").

computedSignal.title: Computed signal
computedSignal.description: A value computed from other signals each time one of its inputs arrives.

expr.title: Expression
expr.description: + - * /, parentheses, decimal constants and signals by key (obd2.<key> for the base set's, such as obd2.map): at most 4 inputs and 16 operations, 256 characters. A computed signal can't read another, or a text one.

max_age.title: Max age
max_age.description: Seconds, 0.1 to 60, per input the expression reads, past which that input is too old to compute from. An input left out takes 3 s.
